sources.title: Practice With Me! Chord Transitions - C & G
sources.why: Close-up of the fretting hand, real-time C<->G switching for ten minutes; the cleanest continuous-play source found.

sources.title: Practice With Me! Chord Transitions - D & G
sources.why: Same player and framing as MtFmLEQ1zoc with a different chord pair: adds D and a second G from the same hand.

sources.title: Chord Switching Practice - C to G
sources.why: A second player and camera for the C/G pair, so a leave-one-video-out fold tests transfer across players.
sources.notes: Instructor talks between drill segments; the audio labeller marks the talk N.

sources.title: Chord Progression Practice - G Em C D
sources.why: A four-chord progression (I-V-vi-IV) from the same player: Em and D on top of G and C.

sources.title: Chord Switching Practice - C to F
sources.why: F is a barre shape: the first non-open shape, and the one most players struggle with.

sources.title: Chord Switching Practice - G to Em
sources.why: G/Em pair from the same player; more Em frames, which the progression video alone gives few of.

sources.title: One Minute Changes - Stage 1
sources.why: The canonical chord-change drill from a third player; stage 1 of that course is A, D and E.
sources.notes: 720p, more talking than the drill channels; the chord list is the course's stage-1 set and is checked by the labeller's per-chord counts.

sources.title: How to play guitar chords - LEFT HANDED absolute beginners
sources.why: A left-handed player: the fretting hand is the right hand and sits on the viewer's left, which the pick and the featurizer must both survive.
sources.notes: Vocabulary is the full open set because the lesson's chord order was not stated in the metadata.

sources.title: C G Am F Play Along Loop
sources.why: A play-along loop with almost no talking: long continuous labelled audio for Am and F.
sources.notes: Camera framing was not verifiable from metadata; kept only if the hand-detection rate after extraction is usable.

sources.title: Matt "Airistotle" Burns (USA) - Air Guitar World Champion 2016
sources.why: Air guitar, no instrument: the domain-shift probe. Never trained on; scored only to see what a real-guitar model does on mimed shapes.
sources.notes: Wide stage shot; the hand is small in frame and detection may fail, which is itself the finding.
